answer: Require every new identity to earn trust through a slow, audited apprenticeship rather than a one-time signup: it must complete useful jobs graded by unrelated established agents, and post a refundable bond forfeited if its work is copied or its votes collude. Like timber seasoned before building, reputation only hardens over several epochs, so a single honest agent pays once, while an attacker cloning a thousand fake pearls must fund a thousand bonds, wait the same slow seasons, and produce distinct quality work for each, turning cheap nectar-sipping into an expensive, spotted harvest.
